_comment: MSV3 fleet registry. Binds each probe's sensor ID to the BLE addresses it is allowed to
appear on and to the bootloader currently installed on it.
Why this file exists: SENSOR_ID is a hand-edited constant in MSV3_Moisture_BLE_Sleep.ino, and
scripts/ble_ota_update.py targets a raw BLE address. Nothing previously connected the two, so
an image built for one probe could be sent to another -- giving two probes the same sensor ID
and silently mixing two plants' data in the receiver. The flasher now resolves --probe N
through this file and refuses any address or package identity that disagrees with it.
application_address is the address the running application advertises on. recovery_address is
application_address + 1, which is where the bootloader advertises when it starts with NO valid
application. After a successful buttonless jump the bootloader instead reuses
application_address, because the peer-data handoff carries it across the reset -- so BOTH
addresses are legitimate bootloader locations and the flasher accepts either.
device_type is the two-byte DFU target tag the installed bootloader accepts: 0x0052 is
Adafruit's stock constant, 0x3356 is what MSV3's own bootloader build replaces it with. It
stops stock-packaged images installing; it is NOT a security property and NOT model-specific.
legacy_package_sha256 allowlists specific pre-65538 application images for one probe. Below
that version the advertised name is not provably equal to the compiled SENSOR_ID, so on a
deployed probe --allow-legacy-package alone is refused; only an image hashed here gets
through. Add one only when deployment records establish that exact image. Empty is correct
when you have no such record -- rebuild instead.
bootloader_key_sha256 pins the SHA-256 of the 64-byte P-256 public point (Qx||Qy) that the
probe's installed bootloader was built to trust. ble_ota_update.py checks the release
manifest's key against it before verifying a signature, so changing the client's trust root
takes a visible edit here as well as to the manifest. 1.0.0 and 1.0.1 share one trust root.
deployed=true means the probe is expected to be advertising, so msv3_fleet_scan.py treats
its absence as a problem. The bench board is deployed=false: it sits powered off most of the
time and its silence says nothing.
'observed' fields record a real scan or transfer, 'inferred' fields have not been seen yet.

installed_application_version is bookkeeping: the bootloader cannot report what it is running. Stock and MSV3 1.0.1 do not enforce it; MSV3 1.0.2+ also records and enforces an on-device anti-rollback floor. ble_ota_update.py independently refuses a package below this value unless --allow-downgrade. Update it after every successful transfer. 0 disables the host-side check.

swd_accessible is MUTABLE PHYSICAL STATE, not history: are this probe's SWD/USB pads reachable RIGHT NOW? Conformal coating makes it false. SET IT FALSE THE MOMENT A PROBE IS COATED -- arduino_msv3_probe.ps1 refuses to build a deliberately-hanging -HangTest image for any probe where this is false, and that refusal is the only thing standing between a coated probe and an image that never opens a radio window.

guard2_validated is a DURABLE FACT and deliberately separate: this hardware has actually demonstrated the watchdog-loop -> BLE DFU escape. Having passed the test once does not make a coated probe recoverable today, so nothing gates on this field; it records what has been proven so a future session does not have to guess.

mbr_params_page_verified is the date UICR.NRFFW[1] was READ ON THIS BOARD and found to hold the MBR params page address (0x000FE000 on nRF52840). Empty/absent means never read. It is the precondition for sending a BOOTLOADER over the air: the bootloader region is rewritten by the MBR via SD_MBR_COMMAND_COPY_BL, which journals into that page so an interrupted copy resumes on the next boot. With the word erased there is no journal and an interrupted copy leaves an unrecoverable board unless SWD can reach it. bootloader_settings.c writes it when blank so it is nearly always set -- 'nearly always' is not a basis for bricking a coated probe, so ble_ota_update.py --bootloader refuses any probe without a date here. Read it per board with the `uicr` command in MSV3_Probe_Bringup_Test; NEVER infer it from a sibling.

probes.notes: The water-immersion board. Migrated off the stock bootloader 2026-09-03 and updated over BLE alone. In soil, battery + solar. Running build 2026-09-05-guard1 (guard 1 only; ENABLE_BOOT_FAILURE_GUARD is staged off until the watchdog-hang test runs with SWD). Confirmed 2026-09-05 00:55 PDT: -72 dBm, 3983 mV, flags 0x1c, DIS reports the build over BLE, receiver ingesting with no false faults. PROVENANCE GAP, recorded 2026-09-05: the exact package installed on this probe was never archived -- it was built into the gitignored .arduino-build/ path, which later builds overwrote, and its source carried an uncommitted SENSOR_ID edit that no commit describes. The running image therefore cannot be reproduced byte-for-byte from this repository. Since 2026-09-05 identity is a build parameter (arduino_msv3_probe.ps1 -SensorId), so (commit, sensor id, build tag) reproduces an image exactly and this cannot recur. Rebuild an equivalent with -SensorId 4 before the next OTA to this probe, and archive the package. This is the battery-powered production unit; final provisioning and coating remain deferred until probes 6 and 7 have exercised the conformal-coating process and functional Probe 6 passes its post-cure check. SOLAR AND CHARGING STATE, measured 2026-09-19: probe 4 sits in the shared Alocasia pot WITH its solar panel. Eight consecutive days 2026-09-06..09-13 show a clean 11:00-16:00 charging ramp of +25 to +90 mV, peaking at 4310 mV, which is the as-built ~4.26 V ceiling. The probe then went off the air on 2026-09-14 -- the R11/R14 rework date -- and returned on 2026-09-18 at 4034 mV. On 2026-09-19 the ramp is GONE: -6 mV across those same hours on the HIGHEST insolation of the entire series (die-temp excursion 8.62 C, against 5.25-7.00 C on the charging days), with wake cadence unchanged at 70 s/wake and the cell falling -53.6 mV/day (r2=0.982). This board RECEIVED the 2026-09-14 rework to 3.887 V nominal VBAT_OV: MSV3_VBAT_OV_STORAGE_REWORK_2026-09-14.md carries a per-board table stating that all field probes EXCEPT MSV3-MOISTURE-007 were swapped on 2026-09-14 (maintainer). That document lives on main (commit edc9705) and NOT on this branch, which is why an earlier version of this note called the rework a hypothesis. It establishes the documented record, not an independent check of the fitted resistors. NOT YET PROVEN: a dead harvester produces identical telemetry. THRESHOLD SEMANTICS -- do not quote a single number. VBAT_OV nominal 3.887 V; on this board ~3.897 V using its own backed-out VBIAS 1.2532 V; ceiling corner band with 1% resistors 3.857-3.937 V; restart is VBAT_OV minus VBAT_OV_HYST whose range is 18/35/89 mV, so the RESTART band is ~3.768-3.919 V, about 151 mV wide. At -53.6 mV/day from 3988 mV the test window is roughly 2026-09-20 to 09-24. Judge it on whether the daytime ramp RETURNS, not on any voltage. WHY IT CURRENTLY READS ABOVE ITS OWN CEILING: the rework did not touch the BQ25170 USB path (R8 = 27k, 4.20 V), and this probe was on USB while off-air 2026-09-14..09-18, so it was charged above the harvester ceiling by a different path and is descending through the dead band. PHYSICAL CHECK from the rework doc: power from the panel with a cell attached and watch VSTOR -- it should plateau near 3.90 V and ripple to ~3.86 V before charging resumes; a probe still stopping near 4.26 V has the resistors reversed or unswapped. SWD ACCESS RE-VERIFIED 2026-09-20 (maintainer, direct statement): this probe's SWD pads are reachable RIGHT NOW. The earlier false value recorded a potted/deployed board, not a coated one; that reason is superseded. Probe 6 remains the ONLY probe whose pads are inaccessible (conformal coating, 2026-09-12). Note this is pad accessibility only -- as of 2026-09-20 the maintainer has no SWD flasher rig configured, so no SWD operation is currently available in practice.

probes.diagnostic_state: 2026-09-21 PROBE 8 IS RUNNING THE BRINGUP DIAGNOSTIC SKETCH, NOT THE PRODUCTION MOISTURE APP. Application v65594, MSV3_Probe_Bringup_Test, build tag bench-session-fix, installed OVER USB with arduino_msv3_probe.ps1 -Action upload (COM9; DFU port auto-discovered as COM19 from the FICR chip serial 1A2F0613682FD239). Restore production firmware before treating any reading from this probe as sensor data: build with -Sketch arduino/MSV3_Moisture_BLE_Sleep and a version above 65594, or re-deliver a release package over BLE. THIS BUILD ADDS THE BENCH FEATURES: a 23-byte 'MSV3'-magic advertisement carrying FDC DATA_CH0, board temperature, bench format version, mux code and FDC STATUS; a `bench on|off` live-broadcast mode that re-reads the FDC and re-advertises every 250 ms; and a connectionless command-beacon scanner that blinks the status LED when the receiver asks. Bluefruit.begin(1, 1) now enables the central slot so BLEScanner can run; the scanner is active ONLY while `bench on` is set and is stopped during any connection, so it cannot disturb a DFU transfer or this sketch's own sleepbench/wakeprofile current measurements. MEASURED 2026-09-21 after this install: 44-packet scan with an advancing wake counter; /bench-data on the receiver reported DATA_CH0 ~39.45M (dry air, as expected for a probe not in soil), board temp 26.0-26.25 C, mux 0, FDC STATUS 0x8, battery ~4307 mV; one POST /bench-identify moved the probe's own accepted/executed counters from 0/0 to 1/1 with last opcode 0x1, proving the replay guard acts exactly once on a beacon that is on air for 2.5 s. The command beacon is 14 bytes and carries a per-receiver-boot SESSION ID at [12-13]: without it the receiver's counter restarts at 1 each boot and collided with the last value this probe had already acted on, which silently dropped the first identify after a receiver reflash (measured). Verified by resetting the receiver alone while the probe held counter 3 -- the next identify advanced it to 4. BOTH FLASHING PATHS REMAIN PROVEN on bootloader msv3-1.0.24. THE ARDUINO IDE UPLOAD BUTTON STILL CANNOT WORK and this is by design, not an outstanding bug -- the IDE and plain arduino-cli build an UNSIGNED package tagged with stock device type 0x0052, which this SIGNED_FW bootloader must refuse, and because single-bank DFU erases the application BEFORE authenticating the init packet, every such attempt costs the probe its firmware and needs a BLE recovery. Use -Action upload instead. USB ENTRY IS THE PRACTICAL CONSTRAINT, not the transport: the production application is duty-cycled and only enumerates USB CDC while awake, so a 1200-baud touch is unreliable against it; the bringup sketch holds the port continuously. For production firmware prefer a double-tap reset then -Action upload -Port <the DFU port>. WHEN LOOKING FOR A PROBE BY COM PORT, MATCH ON THE USB COMPOSITE PARENT. The Ports-class child instance id is a Windows-generated hash and never contains the chip serial; only the parent does (probe 8 = 1A2F0613682FD239, probe 5 = 695715B3A7F8217E). Verified again 2026-09-21: COM9 = probe 8, COM7 = probe 5. Full account: MSV3/docs/MSV3_WIRED_DFU_RESOLVED_2026-09-21.md and DisplayCenter/docs/BENCH_PAGE_AND_COMMAND_BEACON_2026-09-21.md.

shared_outlet.detail: sensor 3 = ESP32-powered v1.2 rig; sensor 9 = ESP32-powered hybrid rig; probe 5 = USB from the computer. All on the same outlet.

isolated.detail: probe 4 = battery only plus solar; sensor 2 = battery.

consequences: DEMOTED 2026-09-19 (maintainer observation): sensors 3 and 9 are BOTH ESP32-powered on the SAME outlet, yet s3 is ~2.9x more thermally immune than s9 (per-day: s3 8.04/9.86/7.54 mV/C vs s9 20.35/21.41/31.20 mV/C against probe 6's room reference). Identical mains exposure, 3x different thermal response -- so mains coupling does NOT explain which rigs are thermally quiet here.

Therefore 'probe 4 is quiet because it is battery-isolated' is a WEAK alternative, not a co-equal explanation. The v1.2 electrode is quiet hardwired (s3) and quiet on battery (probe 4); the blade is noisy hardwired (s9).
STILL CLEAN and now doing double duty: the within-AM comparison (s3 vs s9) is both the load-bearing electrode result and the control that demotes this confound.
STILL WORTH REMOVING: the topology asymmetry is real even if it is not the explanation. Moving probe 5 to battery makes the FDC row power-matched.

_comment: The maintainer's physical reading of what drives noise and thermal drift, stated 2026-09-19.
READ THIS BEFORE ANALYSING THERMAL DATA. It is a TWO-FACTOR model: the readout and the electrode
each contribute their own noise term and their own temperature term, and they are separable.
Sessions have repeatedly tried to force a single-factor answer ('is it the electrode OR the
readout') and got stuck. The answer is BOTH, which is why the apparent electrode effect changes
size depending on which readout it is measured through.
explains: Why the apparent electrode effect changed size with the readout it was measured through (1.36x within the AM pair, ~4x within the FDC pair): the readout adds its own temperature term on top.
Why sensor 3 (v1.2 electrode + v1.2 driving circuit) shows LARGE drift but a LOW thermal coefficient -- noisy circuit, immune electrode.
Why sensor 9 (MSV3 blade + v1.2 driving circuit) shows CLEAN traces with a HIGH thermal coefficient -- low-temp circuit, very-susceptible electrode.
Why probe 4 (v1.2 electrode + FDC) is the flattest rig measured -- low-noise readout AND immune electrode, the best available pairing.
Why probe 4 BEFORE 2026-09-18, when it was MSV3 blade + FDC, was strongly thermal (-0.387 %/C, 2.60% daily swing), and probe 8 on the same pairing wobbled 1.956%.
prediction_probe5: Probe 5 is MSV3 blade + FDC in the shared pot. As of 2026-09-19 it has ~1.5 hours of data, all overnight, so there is NO thermal excursion in it yet. One clean sunny day resolves this.
If the terms add: -0.041 + (-0.346) = -0.387 %/C capacitance, drier when warm, ~2.6% daily swing.

Outcomes: strongly thermal and DRIER when warm -> model holds. Strongly thermal and WETTER -> matches probe 8, so the blade's SIGN is board- or contact-dependent. Near-flat like probe 4 -> the blade term is not an electrode property and an interaction term is needed.

HONEST CAVEAT: existing blade measurements bracket +0.064 to -0.387 %/C, so almost any probe 5 result lands inside that range. One day tests the sign and rough magnitude, NOT the additive form. Establishing additivity needs the electrode crossover (thermal doc, next steps A2).

ANSWERED 2026-09-24, and none of the three listed outcomes was right. Probe 5 measured -0.111 %/C (slightly DRIER when warm) while the soil was dry and +0.545 %/C (strongly WETTER when warm) after the 09-22 watering -- it landed on two different branches of the prediction four days apart. The prediction was mis-specified because it omitted soil water content, which turns out to set both the sign and the magnitude. See tested_2026_09_24.
measurement_model.status: PARTLY SUPERSEDED 2026-09-24. Readout and electrode both contribute, and they INTERACT: the additive form is refuted (tested correctly on differences, see audit). The 'soil water content dominates the temperature term' entry below did NOT survive audit. The dominant daily artifact is the noon sun on the shelf acting on specific installations (sensor 9, probe 7). See tested_2026_09_24.audit below.

tested_2026_09_29.ELECTRODE, NOT CIRCUIT: Same AM detector design, same outlet, same pot and days: the MSV3 blade (sensor 9) swings 29.7% of a watering per day against the v1.2's (sensor 3) 2.6% -- x10.7 paired by day, never below x7.9 on any of 10 days.

AM: crediting ALL of sensor 3's 13.2 mV/day to the shared detector design bounds the circuit at <=21% of sensor 9's 67.3 mV/day (worst day 28%). The MSV3 board in full sun (probe 4, die ~8 C, battery + solar in circuit) driving a v1.2 swings only 6.6% of a watering.
tested_2026_09_29.QUALIFICATION: The blade's swing is an installation property, not a fixed blade coefficient: probe 5 (blade + FDC, the only SHADE-side rig) is 3.8%, no worse than the v1.2s (per C of own die range: p5 0.70, p4 0.77 % of a watering). audit.STANDS: Watering-step normalization (the maintainer states the pot saturates uniformly). Blade + AM (sensor 9) is the worst Alocasia rig. Readout and electrode interact: blade minus v1.2 is -2.49 pp via the FDC and +24.25 pp via the AM. SNR ordering, from one event.

audit.DOES NOT STAND: 'soil water is the dominant temperature factor' and 'the sign inversion is a moisture effect'. Both used a per-day linear detrend that the post-watering dry-down contaminates. In a joint fit: probe 5 PRE +0.041 (no sign flip) and POST +0.433. Probe 4 rose no more than the no-soil control (+0.10 vs +0.12). Probe 7 rose x1.2 only. The AM rigs read DRIER when warm before and after. The probe 4 (-0.387) vs probe 8 puzzle is NOT retired.
audit.DOES NOT STAND 2: Probe 7's '+2.99 step' and the 90x / 427.6% / SNR 0.27 ratios built on it. The +2.99 is inside probe 7's night-to-night scatter (sd 4.2). With sun and room modelled out, probe 7's watering step is +5.1 logC%, above every placebo day, so it DID see the watering.
audit.NEW: The daily artifact is the NOON SUN reaching the shelf (~11:50-12:10 PDT). The +2 h response as % of each rig's watering step: sensor 9 -17%, probe 7 larger than its watering, probes 4/5 and sensor 3 ~0.8%, sensor 2 1.8%. Sensor 9 follows room air with little lag; probe 7 follows the sun with a 2-4 h lag. Probe 7 was flipped to face the soil 2026-09-24 ~23:17 PDT to test the maintainer's facing-direction theory: MSV3/docs/MSV3_PROBE7_FLIP_TEST_2026-09-24.md.

_comment: The 2026-09-22 watering gave every rig in a pot one common physical input, which is the
transfer calibration all earlier work lacked. Dividing each rig's thermal artifact by its
OWN watering step makes AM mV, FDC counts and MSV2 LSB comparable for the first time.
READ THIS BEFORE RANKING ELECTRODES OR READOUTS ON A RAW THERMAL COEFFICIENT.
tested_2026_09_24.source: MSV3/scripts/analyze_alocasia_watering.py over 190 h of raw cloud history, receiver MSV2088A3104A7AC
tested_2026_09_24.REFUTED -- the additive form: The blade's normalized thermal penalty is x0.66 through the FDC readout (probe 4 vs probe 5, shared pot, 09-23/24) and x10.73 through the AM readout (sensors 3 vs 9, shared pot, four days). Same two electrode types, same soil, same days, 16x apart. The readout and electrode INTERACT. Any compensation using one signed coefficient per readout plus one per electrode will fail.
tested_2026_09_24.NEW -- soil water is the dominant temper: Every probe with an electrode in soil got a LARGER coefficient across the watering (probe 4 x2.2, probe 7 x1.8, probe 5 flipped sign from -0.111 to +0.545 %/C). Probe 6, in no soil, did not move: +0.066 -> +0.070 -> +0.088 %/C, which is also the board's own floor. Post-watering every in-soil rig reads WETTER WHEN WARM, consistent with ionic conductivity reaching the FDC as Maxwell-Wagner apparent capacitance.
tested_2026_09_24.RESOLVED -- the sign inversion is a mois: Probe 5 read -0.111 %/C dry and +0.545 %/C wet: same board, same electrode, same pot, four days apart. The sign is NOT a board or contact property. Retire the 'the blade inverts the sign and it is board-dependent' hypothesis, and with it the probe 4 (-0.387) vs probe 8 (+0.064) puzzle.
tested_2026_09_24.NEW -- installation dominates electrode: Probe 5 and probe 7 are both MSV3 blade + FDC2214. Normalized artifact 4.75% of a watering step versus 427.6% -- a 90x spread with electrode and readout held fixed, at comparable die excursions. 'MSV3 blade + FDC' is not one thing, and no coefficient measured on one installation transfers to another.
tested_2026_09_24.REFRAMED -- the blade is not a net liabi: Through the FDC the blade costs x1.87 thermal artifact but buys x2.85 signal, so it is net BETTER. The earlier framing judged the blade on its raw coefficient without dividing by what that coefficient pays for.
tested_2026_09_24.WORST PAIRING -- blade + AM: Sensor 9 loses signal (x0.45) AND gains artifact (x4.81) against sensor 3. The only pairing bad on both counts; SNR 3.7 against sensor 3's 40.2. Do not carry blade + AM into MSV4.
tested_2026_09_24.SNR ranking, step divided by one day of: sensor 3 v1.2+AM 40.2; probe 5 blade+FDC 22.1; probe 4 v1.2+FDC 18.3; sensor 2 MSV2 RC 9.6; sensor 9 blade+AM 3.7; probe 7 blade+FDC Begonia 0.27.
tested_2026_09_24.INFERRED, not measured: That the blade OVER-LOADS the AM detector. Supporting evidence: sensor 9 sits at 1864 mV predawn against sensor 3's 2422 mV, and its relative gain is 0.85 over the 6-day dry-down but 0.45 over the watering -- gain collapsing at the wet, heavily-loaded end. Two regimes is evidence, not proof; a swept-load bench measurement of detector gain would settle it.
tested_2026_09_24.SAMPLE SIZE: ONE watering event. The spread between rigs is far larger than any plausible error, but every normalized figure rests on one step per rig. Re-derive at the next watering, and RECORD THE WATER VOLUME and pot mass -- without them no step here is a calibrated sensitivity.

tested_2026_09_19: SUPPORTED -- 'FDC readout is temperature-susceptible': probe 4's BARE TANK, with the electrode physically disconnected, is r=-0.994 at -0.041 %/C. Real and almost perfectly thermal, but ~8x smaller than the blade's contribution.

WITHDRAWN as cross-pot (maintainer, 2026-09-19) -- the 3.7x blade-vs-v1.2 ratio subtracted probe 4's blade term (its OWN pot, 09-05..09-09) from its v1.2 term (SHARED pot, 09-19). Different soil on each side. This also re-explains the probe 4 vs probe 8 blade disagreement as two POTS, not two boards. What survives: the within-AM 2.9x (sensors 3 and 9, same pot, same days), and the readout term below which touches no soil.

SUPPORTED, PARTIALLY -- 'the v1.2 driving circuit is noisy': sensors 3 and 9 have essentially identical noise (0.80 vs 0.92 LSB RMS) despite different electrodes, so the noise is a CIRCUIT property. Ranking FDC against the v1.2 circuit is NOT possible without the detector's mV-per-pF slope; sensor 3 is also quantization-limited at 37 LSB per day.

NOT ESTABLISHED -- the ADDITIVE form. The blade term is not reproducible across boards: probe 4 (blade+FDC, own pot) measured -0.387 %/C while probe 8 (blade+FDC, shared pot) measured +0.064 %/C. Opposite signs, 6x magnitude. Either something uncontrolled matters (soil contact, insertion depth, orientation) or the terms interact rather than add.
NEW -- the electrode INVERTS the sign within one readout, it does not merely scale. Any compensation assuming a single signed coefficient per readout will fail.
comparison_rules: NEVER compare a probe's data across a pot change. See pots.shared-alocasia.insertion_dates for each sensor's entry date.
VERIFIED 2026-09-19: the within-AM 2.9x (sensors 3 vs 9, 09-17..09-19) IS clean. Sensor 3 has been in this pot throughout and sensor 9 entered 09-14 18:30, both well before that window.
WITHDRAWN: any ratio built by subtracting probe 4's own-pot blade data from its shared-pot v1.2 data. Different soil on each side.

SETTLING CAVEAT: probe 4 entered 2026-09-18 20:53 and its +0.053 %/C v1.2 figure comes from the FIRST ~18 HOURS after insertion. Probe 5 entered 2026-09-19 ~20:24. Neither is at steady state yet; re-measure both after several days before treating either number as the electrode's property.
The REAL electrode measurement is probe 4 vs probe 5 once both have settled: same pot, same soil, same FDC readout, same days, one variable.
Bare-tank figures are pot-independent (electrode disconnected, no soil contact) and are the only ones safe to carry across pot changes.

ADDED 2026-09-24: NEVER rank electrodes or readouts on a raw thermal coefficient. Divide each rig's artifact by its OWN watering step first. Doing so reverses the blade verdict through the FDC readout, because the blade's larger coefficient buys more than it costs. The step is the only common calibration between AM mV, FDC counts and MSV2 LSB.

ADDED 2026-09-24: a thermal coefficient is only comparable between rigs AT THE SAME SOIL WATER CONTENT. Probe 5 moved from -0.111 to +0.545 %/C across one watering. Never compare a pre-watering coefficient with a post-watering one, and never pool days across a watering in one fit.
